name: Papeete Centre
tagline: The market, the waterfront and the roulottes
description: The centre of the city around the Marché de Papeete, a two-storey covered market selling fish, fruit, vanilla and monoi, with the waterfront where the roulottes food trucks set up every evening. It is walkable and it is where Tahiti works.
bestFor: Anyone who wants the market, the ferries and the city's services
pros: The market and the roulottes on the quay
cons: Not a beach city in any sense

name: Punaauia and the West Coast
tagline: South of the city, where the beaches are
description: The coast running southwest from Papeete, with the island's best accessible beaches at Plage de Vaiava and the Museum of Tahiti and Her Islands, plus much of the residential development that serves the capital. Lagoon swimming is calm here.
bestFor: Longer stays wanting a beach and a commute into Papeete
pros: The best beaches within reach of the city
Museum of Tahiti and Her Islands
cons: Heavy traffic into Papeete at peak
Twenty to thirty minutes from the centre

name: Moorea
tagline: Thirty minutes by ferry, and a different island
description: The island visible across the water from Papeete, reached by a constant ferry in half an hour, with two deep bays, a mountainous interior and lagoon water the capital does not have. A great many people who work in Papeete live here instead.
bestFor: Anyone who wants Tahiti's infrastructure and Moorea's setting
pros: Cook's and Opunohu bays and the Belvedere
cons: The ferry is a daily commitment

name: The Presqu'ile and Teahupo'o
tagline: The far end of Tahiti, and the wave
description: The smaller peninsula joined to the main island by an isthmus, greener, wetter and far less developed, ending at Teahupo'o where one of the heaviest waves in the world breaks over a shallow reef. The road stops before the village ends.
bestFor: Surfers and anyone who wants Tahiti without the traffic
pros: Teahupo'o and the surf culture around it
cons: An hour or more from Papeete
Wetter than the northwest of the island

name: The Tuamotus (atolls, 450 km northeast by air)
tagline: The atolls, an hour away by air
description: The chain of low coral atolls east of Tahiti, with Rangiroa and Fakarava the best known, where the passes between ocean and lagoon carry enormous concentrations of fish and sharks. Fakarava is a UNESCO biosphere reserve.
bestFor: Divers, for whom this is the reason to come to French Polynesia at all
pros: Among the best diving in the world
The Fakarava grouper aggregation in June and July
cons: Expensive to reach and to stay
